scenario.case_file: Ben Hartley, 36, was dropped at the Mount Hood Meadows trailhead intending a day hike and did not return. Vehicle is at Mount Hood Meadows.

late_evidence.text: A second party at the trailhead recalls someone matching Ben Hartley's description accepting a lift mid-morning from a vehicle that left heading north-east.

frames.trigger_reason: 53% of the mass predicted by 'Lost hiker, down-drainage' has been covered with no contact

nominations.label: Lifted to NE side
nominations.narrative: Ben was picked up by a vehicle heading north‑east from the trailhead and was taken to the lower‑elevation area on the far side of the divide (near the 49° bearing).
nominations.rationale: Witness report of a lift mid‑morning from a vehicle heading north‑east indicates Ben was moved away from the planning point. The lowest ground lies to the north‑east, so the lift likely placed him on that side of the massif.
evidence_cited: A second party at the trailhead recalls someone matching Ben Hartley's description accepting a lift mid‑morning from a vehicle that left heading north‑east.
The lowest ground in the operating area lies to the north‑east (bearing 49), where the drainages run out.

nominations.label: Transported to far side via lift
nominations.narrative: Ben was transported by the same vehicle to the far side of the divide, beyond the high point of the massif, effectively starting the search at the back side of the mountain.
nominations.rationale: The witness description of the ‘back side’ or ‘other side of the divide’ implies a location on the far side of the massif. A vehicle lift could easily move Ben there, placing his true starting point roughly 8 km away at bearing 315.
evidence_cited: The far side of the massif – what a witness would call 'the back side' or 'the other side of the divide' – is reached by continuing on bearing 135 past the summit, roughly 2 km from the planning point
